artworks.title: Henricus a Zijll
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man's upper body. He is positioned in a semi-profile view, turned slightly to his left. The man has a calm expression with well-defined facial features, including a prominent nose and mustache, and his hair is short and neatly combed back. He is wearing elaborate clothing typical of the period, featuring a richly patterned, fur-lined cloak, and a large, starched ruff collar around his neck. The background of the portrait consists of a textured, crosshatched pattern. Below the image, there is an inscription in Latin.

artworks.title: Coat of Arms in a Circle
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a heraldic shield featuring a coat of arms. The image shows an intricate coat of arms centrally placed within a circular shape. Symbols of lions and diverse patterns adorn the shield, which is surrounded by a crown at the top. The circle has an inscription that seems to read "HONI SOIT QUI MAL Y PENSE," a motto related to chivalry. The artwork showcases intricate line work, emphasizing the texture of the lions, patterns within the shield, and decorations around the edge.

artworks.title: Coat of Arms, Moniti Meliora
artworks.description: The image shows an engraving of a ship at sea. The ship is centrally positioned, with billowing sails, flanked by two columns. In the background, smaller vessels can be seen on the horizon. Above the scene, there is an elaborate coat of arms supported by two figures, surrounded by clouds. The engraving features fine lines, emphasizing texture and form, with a monochromatic palette of black, white, and grey. The sea is depicted as choppy with curling waves, and ornate details enhance the classical style of the artwork.

artworks.title: Bookplate for Ambrose Isted
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a coat of arms. The image shows a shield adorned with decorative elements and a motto. A helmet with ornamentation is placed above the shield, with a stag's head wearing a crown emerging from the top. The shield contains patterns of triangles and dog heads arranged in a triangular fashion. A ribbon below the shield displays the inscription "NOSCE TEIP SUM," and the name "Ambrose Isted Esq." is written at the bottom, surrounded by decorative embellishments.

artworks.title: Coat of Arms of Howard, Duke of Norfolk
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a heraldic coat of arms. The image features a shield divided into four quadrants with different patterns and symbols, and flanked by a lion and a unicorn as supporters. Above the shield is a helmet topped with a crown, with foliage extending into decorative mantling. Atop the crown sits a lion. A banner below the shield reads "SOLI VIRTUS INVICTA," and "Howard Duke of Norfolk" is inscribed below. The artwork showcases intricate line work typical of traditional heraldic illustrations.

artworks.title: Coat of Arms of Prince Rupert, Hollar and Evelyn
Title Page of Book by Alleyne, Lord St. Helens
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a historical document with a coat of arms. The document contains French text related to Alleyne Lord St. Helens and their roles with the British monarchy and the Russian emperor. A heraldic coat of arms is depicted at the top, featuring a lion and a unicorn on either side of a shield with insignia and a crown. A ribbon below the lion reads "DIEU ET MON DROIT." Additional decoration and the name Lord St. Helens can be seen in smaller print at the bottom left. The document appears to date back to 1802 and is printed on aged, cream-colored paper that has darkened at the edges.

artworks.title: Coat of Arms of Shakespeare
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a coat of arms. The image features two heraldic shields: the top shield has a diagonal stripe with a spear, accompanied by the motto "NON SANZ DROICT," and is crowned by a crest depicting an eagle holding a spear. The bottom shield is divided vertically, with the left side mirroring the spear stripe of the top shield, while the right side contains three objects resembling cross-crosslets. The document is titled "The Arms of Shakspere," and there is a note at the bottom indicating it was printed in London by J. Bell in 1787 for the British Library Strand.

artworks.title: Title Page for the Achievement of our Soveraigne King James
artworks.description: This is a black and white illustration of a complex heraldic composition. The image features a central coat of arms surrounded by various symbols, mythical creatures, and smaller shields with distinct imagery. Cherubs appear to be holding a curtain above the central coat of arms. An inscription at the bottom references "the achievement of our sovereign King James." The drawing conveys grandeur and historical significance.

artworks.title: Title Page for the Achievement of our Soveraigne King James
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a heraldic composition featuring the Coat of Arms of King James I. The central part of the image depicts an ornate coat of arms surrounded by mythological shield bearers and a detailed border containing several smaller coats of arms.

artworks.title: Title Page to Angleterre
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a decorative title page for a book about England. The artwork features an elaborate heraldic design at the top, showcasing a shield with three lions, surrounded by a crowned lion on the left and a mythical creature resembling a winged dragon on the right. Above the shield, rays of light emanate down from above. Below the heraldry, there are architectural elements resembling a classical building facade with niches housing statues of armed and armored figures labeled "ROMANVS," "NORMANNVS," "BRITANNVS," "SAXO," and "DANVS." The central area has a draped fabric backdrop that frames more text: "ANGLETERRE, QVI EST LE XI. LIVRE DE L'EUROPE." The artist has skillfully used shading and line work to create depth and a sense of grandeur fitting the subject matter.

artworks.title: Title Page for the Achievement of Our Sovereign King Charles the Second
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a decorative coat of arms for King Charles II of England. The full description includes a central shield with multiple heraldic symbols, topped with a crown and sided by a lion and a unicorn as supporters. Surrounding the main coat of arms is a wide border filled with smaller shields representing the arms of various royal dynasties and regions historically connected to or ruled by the monarchy in England. At the bottom, a banner bears the motto "DIEU ET MON DROIT." The artwork features intricate detail and symmetry typical of 17th-century heraldic art.

artworks.title: Title Page to Atlas Novus by William and JohnBlaev
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a title page for an atlas. The page features a coat of arms at the top, supported by a lion and a dragon. Beneath it, there is a central figure labeled "BRITANNVS" holding a spear, flanked by three other figures labeled "ROMANVS", "DANVS", "SAXO", and "NORMANNVS". The lower section of the page includes inscriptions in Latin, the title of the atlas "THEATRUM ORBIS TERRARVM, sive ATLAS NOVVS" and publication details. The style of the drawing suggests a historical and scholarly theme, suitable for an important atlas frontispiece.

artworks.title: Title page, Baziliologia
artworks.description: The image features an intricate engraving with a full-length depiction of a regal figure on the left, holding a scepter. To the right, another figure in armor stands in a dynamic pose. In the center is a text panel with floral and scroll elements. Above it is a figure blowing a trumpet and holding scales, perched atop architectural elements. Flanking this figure are two circular portrait medallions, one of a bearded man and one of a woman. The background includes scenes of battle and figures in motion, rich in symbolic and heraldic imagery.

artworks.title: Title Page to Clarissimi IV
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a decorative text page. The page features intricate and detailed artwork surrounding and incorporating text sections. It includes symmetrical columns of ornate scrollwork and classical motifs on both sides, containing panels with carved figures and faces. Above the central text is a detailed vignette showing a scene of individuals gathered around a seated figure in a semi-lit environment. Additional smaller illustrations, including archers with bows aiming outward, decorate the top area of the design. The use of Latin text and elaborate framing suggests a work intended to convey authority and knowledge. At the bottom is the year "M. D. XXXII," indicating 1532 in Roman numerals.

artworks.title: Title Page to De Republicae Anglorum by Thomas Chaloner
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a historical book cover or title page. The image displays a title page from a book printed in 1579. The typography is in Latin, featuring the title "DE REP. ANGLORUM INSTAURANDA LIBRI DECEM" and the author's name "Thoma Chalonero." Additional Latin text is present, likely describing the contents or additional works by the same author. Below the text is an intricate coat of arms or emblem enclosed in an oval, decorated with floral motifs and Latin inscriptions. It states that the book was printed in London by Thomas Vautrollier. The page has a well-preserved, aged appearance, characteristic of printed works from the 16th century.

artworks.title: Title Page to "The Theatre of the Empire of Great Britaine" by John Speed
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a detailed historical title page design. The illustration features an architectural-style frame with various decorative elements. Within the frame is a central figure standing on a pedestal, holding a spear and a shield. Surrounding this central figure are smaller niches containing figures dressed in historical, military attire, each identified with labels. The title block in the lower central part reads "The Theatre of the Empire of Great Britaine," credited to John Speed and dated 1611. The surrounding decorations include intricate patterns, heraldic symbols, and small statues, reflecting a sense of grandeur and stately antiquity from the early 17th century. The composition aims to depict a historical narrative through detailed and symbolic imagery.

artworks.title: Title Page to "The Theatre of the Empire of Great Britaine" by John Speed
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an elaborate title page. The page is decorated with classical architectural elements such as pillars, arches, and motifs. In the center, there is a large arch framing a central figure with a shield and staff, above the words "Britannia." Surrounding this are additional arched niches with figures labeled as "A Romane," "A Dane," "A Saxon," and "A Norman," each depicted in period-appropriate attire and armed with swords and shields. Above the central arch are two smaller figures in dynamic poses. In the middle of the page are the words "THE THEATRE OF THE EMPIRE OF GREAT BRITAINE" and text detailing an "exact geography" of England, Scotland, Ireland, and nearby isles. The document is imprinted at London in 1611. The border includes various crests, masks, and foliage, enhancing the design. The composition is detailed with fine line work, showcasing intricate attention to detail and classical design elements from the early 17th century.

artworks.title: Title Page to "The Theatre of the Empire of Great Britaine" by John Speed
artworks.artist: Robert White after Jodocus Hondius I
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an architectural facade with allegorical figures. The engraving shows detailed arches and columns, surrounding figures representing historical peoples associated with Great Britain. In the center is a figure of Britannia holding a spear and shield. Above the central arch is a medallion labeled "BRITAIN". Flanking Britannia are figures labeled "A ROMANE" and "A SAXON" above, and "A DANE" and "A NORMAN" below. Between them is an inscribed space titled "THE THEATRE OF THE EMPIRE OF GREAT BRITAINE" by John Speed. Decorative elements include cherubs and shields carved into the architectural details.

artworks.title: Title page to Holland's "Herwologia"
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring a central large oval cartouche filled with Latin text, flanked by architectural and classical figures. Above the cartouche, a cherubic figure, flanked by two seated figures, holds an image of a map labeled "Angliae brevis descriptio." Two main figures are seated on pedestals, one holding a staff and the other holding a pen and a scroll. Latin inscriptions along the top depict relevant quotations or mottos. Below the central text, there is a smaller detailed cartouche depicting the cityscape of London, labeled as "Londini." The style is reminiscent of classical allegories and iconography, emphasizing harmony and symmetry in the arrangement of text and figures. The detailed lines, hatching, and textures show the draughtsman's skill.

artworks.title: Title page, An History of the Civill Warres of England
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a detailed and ornate title page for a historical text. The central oval plaque bears the title "An history of the civil warres of England between the two houses of Lancaster and Yorke." Above the title is a figure of a seated person with wings playing a trumpet. To the sides are ornate medallions featuring portraits labeled with Latin script. Below the medallions stand two figures; one on the left is dressed in regal robes and a crown, the other on the right in armor. The base of the composition includes a battlefield scene with soldiers in traditional armor. The style is formal and classical, suggesting a historical theme. The intricate line work indicates that the drawing may have been created as an engraving.

artworks.title: Title Page to "The History of Great Britaine" by John Speed
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an elaborate title page for "The History of Great Britaine". The illustration serves as a decorative framing for the text detailing the book's contents. The central figure is a classical warrior holding a staff and shield standing in an arched alcove. Surrounding this figure are detailed architectural elements reminiscent of classical Roman structures. Each side of the central figure features three smaller alcoves, each containing a Roman, Saxon, Dane, and Norman figure. Ornate decorative elements fill the space above and below, incorporating shields, helmets, and classical iconography. The text "The History of Great Britaine" is prominently displayed on the page.

artworks.title: Title Page to Saturne Ephemerides by Henry Isaacson
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an ornate title page. It features an elaborate frame with columns, scrolls, and text. The central panel is labeled "Saturni Ephemerides" with intricate text. Two columns on either side have globes on their tops. Three figures are depicted above the text. In the lower panel, there is a depiction of a pyramid with workers surrounding it. The drawing is detailed and crafted with fine lines.

artworks.title: Title Page to Urbium Praecipuarum Totius Mundi
artworks.description: This painting depicts an allegorical representation with a central figure of Justice. Various personifications and symbols are arranged in a classical architectural structure. Justice is in the center wearing a red cloak, holding a sword and scales. Surrounding her are other allegories like Peace and Concordia, each represented by women with attributes such as a caduceus and a wreath. A bull's skull decorates the top of the arch with a garland. Below, a large plaque with Latin text is framed by personifications like Community, Obedience, and Security. The background features a depiction of a tower similar to the Tower of Babel. The intricate details, rich colors, and classical columns create a sense of grandeur and mythological significance. This is in the style of an artist like Maarten de Vos, who often combines allegorical and classical themes in his works.
